key_factors: Scotland's form is exceptional: 8 goals across 2 warm-up wins from multiple different scorers
Scott McTominay confirmed fully fit despite stomach illness scare — key midfield engine available
Steve Clarke has his only lineup question mark as who partners McKenna at CB — otherwise settled
Haiti's 4-0 win over New Zealand is real — Isidor and Bellegarde are dangerous on transitions
Billy Gilmour's injury (replaced by Tyler Fletcher) is the one genuine concern for midfield depth
reasoning: Scotland arrive at their first World Cup in 28 years playing their best football in years. Four goals against both Curaçao and Bolivia demonstrates clinical finishing from multiple sources — Shankland, McTominay, Adams. Clarke's tactical clarity — settled back four, McTominay as the driving force, Robertson bombing forward — should overwhelm Haiti's compact 4-4-2. Haiti showed against New Zealand they can score, so Scotland's defence must guard against cheap goals. But a 2-0 win is the most probable result: Scotland have too much quality for Haiti to contain for 90 minutes.
